foodie.title: Whiskey Flight at Teeling Distillery
foodie.description: The first new distillery to open in Dublin in over a century — walk the copper stills in the Liberties, then taste three side by side.
foodie.bonus: Pick your favourite before they tell you the prices.

foodie.title: Dinner at Etto on Merrion Row
foodie.description: A narrow Italian-leaning room with a wine list far better than the size of the place suggests and food that never overreaches.
foodie.bonus: Let them pair the wine by the glass.

foodie.title: Two Michelin Stars at Liath
foodie.description: Twenty-odd seats inside Blackrock Market serving one of the most quietly ambitious tasting menus in Ireland.
foodie.bonus: Book the counter, not the table.

foodie.title: Chips from Leo Burdock, Eaten Standing Up
foodie.description: Take a bag of cod and chips from the Werburgh Street counter and eat them off the paper on the steps of Christ Church.

foodie.title: Lobster Roll at Klaw
foodie.description: A tiny no-reservations crab shack off Temple Bar doing Irish shellfish fast, cold and buttery at a shared counter.
foodie.bonus: Add the hot sauce they make in-house.

foodie.title: Bunsen: Burger, Fries, Nothing Else
foodie.description: The menu fits on a business card because there are four things on it, and all four are the point.
foodie.bonus: Order exactly what the person before you ordered.

foodie.title: Coffee Nerdery at 3fe
foodie.description: The roastery that dragged Irish coffee culture into the present — order the filter and let them talk you through it.
foodie.bonus: Ask what they are most excited about right now.

foodie.title: Long Breakfast at The Fumbally
foodie.description: A high-ceilinged Dublin 8 warehouse café where nobody rushes you and the eggs come with things you did not expect.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever is chalked up rather than off the menu.

foodie.title: Oysters and a pint at The Brazen Head
foodie.description: Crack open a dozen oysters at Ireland's oldest pub, pouring since 1198, with a stout to wash it down.
foodie.bonus: Ask the bartender which whiskey pairs best with oysters.

foodie.title: Brunch at Brother Hubbard North
foodie.description: Order straight off the daily specials board at this Middle Eastern-leaning brunch spot loved by Dublin locals.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever's on the daily specials board, no menu-reading allowed.

foodie.title: Cheese and charcuterie tasting at Sheridans Cheesemongers
foodie.description: Taste your way across a counter piled with Irish farmhouse cheeses and cured meats, one wedge at a time.
foodie.bonus: Ask for the strongest cheese on the counter and try it first.

foodie.title: Tasting menu at Chapter One
foodie.description: Sit down for a Michelin-starred tasting menu in a basement dining room beneath the Dublin Writers Museum.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to surprise you with the pairing.

culture.title: Kilmainham Gaol, Cell by Cell
culture.description: The guided tour through the prison where the 1916 leaders were held and executed, ending in the stonebreakers' yard.
culture.bonus: Book weeks ahead — it sells out constantly.

culture.title: A Play at the Abbey
culture.description: Ireland's national theatre, founded by Yeats and Lady Gregory, still programming new Irish writing rather than trading on the back catalogue.
culture.bonus: Read nothing about the play before you go in.

culture.title: Chained Books at Marsh's Library
culture.description: Ireland's first public library, opened 1707 and essentially unchanged — dark oak stalls, and wire cages readers were once locked into with the rare books.
culture.bonus: Find the bullet holes from 1916 in the shelves.

culture.title: Contemporary Art in a 17th-Century Hospital
culture.description: IMMA sits inside the Royal Hospital Kilmainham, so the collection hangs in colonnaded rooms built for retired soldiers in 1684.
culture.bonus: Walk the formal gardens behind the building afterwards.

culture.title: EPIC and the Emigrant Story
culture.description: Twenty vaulted rooms under the CHQ building tracing where ten million people went after they left, and what they did when they got there.
culture.bonus: Look up whether your own surname is on the wall.

culture.title: The Glasnevin Cemetery Tour
culture.description: A genuinely gripping walk through 1.5 million graves — Collins, Parnell, de Valera — told as the history of modern Ireland in one field.
culture.bonus: Climb the O'Connell Tower for the view over the city.

culture.title: Bloomsday in Costume
culture.description: Every 16 June the city re-enacts a single day in 1904 — straw hats, kidney for breakfast, and readings on the street corners where they happen in the book.
culture.bonus: Eat the Gorgonzola sandwich and burgundy at Davy Byrnes.

culture.title: Stand in Front of the Caravaggio
culture.description: The National Gallery holds The Taking of Christ, lost for two centuries and found hanging unrecognised in a Jesuit dining room on Leeson Street.
culture.bonus: Find the painter's own face in the painting.

adventure.title: Ticknock's Fairy Castle Loop
adventure.description: A short, steep climb through pine forest to a cairn on the Dublin Mountains with the whole bay laid out beneath you.
adventure.bonus: Do it at dusk and watch the city lights come on.

adventure.title: Chase Powerscourt Waterfall
adventure.description: Drive an hour south into Wicklow for Ireland's highest waterfall, a 121-metre drop into a beech valley you can picnic under.
adventure.bonus: Get close enough that the spray soaks you.

adventure.title: Learn to Sail on Dublin Bay
adventure.description: Take a taster keelboat session out of Dún Laoghaire harbour and spend an afternoon actually working the sheets rather than sitting still.
adventure.bonus: Take the helm for at least one full tack.

adventure.title: Walk the Bray to Greystones Cliff Path
adventure.description: Follow the old railway path carved into the sea cliffs from Bray Head to Greystones, then take the DART back with your legs aching.
adventure.bonus: Swim at the Greystones end before the train home.

adventure.title: Summit Lugnaquilla, Wicklow's Highest Point
adventure.description: A full day on the highest ground in Leinster, climbing out of Glenmalure to a flat summit plateau where the weather changes on you.
adventure.bonus: Sign the summit box at the top.

adventure.title: Kayak Out to Dalkey Island
adventure.description: Paddle out of Bulloch Harbour to the ruined church and wild goats of Dalkey Island, with seals surfacing beside the boat the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Land on the island and touch the Martello tower.

adventure.title: Trad Climb at Dalkey Quarry
adventure.description: Rope up on the granite where every Irish climber learned, twenty minutes from the city and hanging right over the sea.
adventure.bonus: Top out and stay for the view over Killiney Bay.

adventure.title: Ride the Royal Canal Greenway Out of Town
adventure.description: Pick up the towpath behind Croke Park and cycle west until the city turns into locks, swans and empty water.
adventure.bonus: Ride until you can no longer hear traffic.

adventure.title: Indoor climb at Awesome Walls Climbing Centre
adventure.description: Work your way up bouldering walls and roped routes at one of Dublin's biggest climbing gyms.
adventure.bonus: Send a route one grade harder than you'd normally try.

adventure.title: Hike the Wicklow Way to Glendalough's Upper Lake
adventure.description: Climb through the Wicklow Mountains past a sixth-century monastic settlement to a glacial lake ringed by cliffs.
adventure.bonus: Reach the monastic round tower before starting the climb up.

adventure.title: Run the full loop of Phoenix Park
adventure.description: Run the perimeter of one of Europe's largest enclosed city parks, past grazing deer and the President's residence.
adventure.bonus: Spot the wild deer herd near Fifteen Acres.

adventure.title: Kayak the River Liffey through the city center
adventure.description: Paddle a guided route straight through Dublin's docklands, gliding under bridges most tourists only ever see from above.
adventure.bonus: Paddle under at least four of the Liffey's bridges.

adventure.title: Sunrise sea swim at the Forty Foot
adventure.description: Join the locals who swim year-round off this famous rocky platform where the water is bracing no matter the season.
adventure.bonus: Swim without a wetsuit, no matter the season.

adventure.title: Cycle the Great South Wall to Poolbeg Lighthouse
adventure.description: Ride the flat sea wall out past the power station stacks to a red lighthouse standing alone at the harbor mouth.
adventure.bonus: Ride all the way to the red lighthouse at the end.

adventure.title: Walk the Howth Head cliff loop
adventure.description: Circle the rugged headland on a coastal trail with gorse-covered cliffs on one side and open Irish Sea on the other.
adventure.bonus: Spot a seal near the harbor before you start the trail.

social.title: Race Night at Leopardstown
social.description: Summer evening racing south of the city where half of Dublin turns up for the last three races and the band that plays after them.
social.bonus: Put a fiver on the horse with the best name.

social.title: Ring the Bell at the Vintage Cocktail Club
social.description: An unmarked door in Crown Alley with a brass bell — ring it, get let in, and drink in a room that pretends the last sixty years did not happen.
social.bonus: Order something you cannot pronounce off the vintage list.

social.title: A Gig at Whelan's
social.description: The Wexford Street venue every Irish band has played on the way up — buy a ticket for whoever is on without checking who they are.
social.bonus: Stay for the support act's whole set.

social.title: Comedy Cellar, Upstairs at the International
social.description: Dublin's longest-running comedy club, confusingly held in the upstairs room of a Wicklow Street pub, where most Irish comics cut their teeth.
social.bonus: Sit in the front row and accept the consequences.

social.title: The Long Hall on a Sunday
social.description: Chandeliers, red velvet and carved mahogany on South Great George's Street, poured slowly and without a hint of irony.
social.bonus: Count the clocks behind the bar.

social.title: Grogan's, a Toastie and No Music
social.description: The artists' pub off South William Street: paintings for sale on the walls, a famous ham and cheese toastie, and deliberately no soundtrack.
social.bonus: Sit outside on the kerb like everyone else does.

social.title: A Pint of Plain at Kehoe's
social.description: A Victorian bar with snugs, a grocery counter that never left, and upstairs rooms that still feel like someone's flat.
social.bonus: Get the snug if it is free. Guard it.

social.title: Sunset in the Gravity Bar
social.description: Ride up through seven floors of the old fermentation plant to a glass drum with a 360-degree view and a pint waiting at the top.
social.bonus: Pick out Howth Head and the Wicklow Mountains from the glass.

social.title: Live trad session at The Cobblestone
social.description: Squeeze into a packed corner of this Smithfield pub for an unamplified, unscripted traditional Irish music session.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the musicians if you love the set.

social.title: Match day at Croke Park for a GAA game
social.description: Feel 80,000 fans roar at once inside Europe's third-largest stadium for a hurling or Gaelic football championship game.
social.bonus: Learn one Irish phrase from the fans around you and use it.

social.title: Pub crawl through Temple Bar
social.description: Bounce between the cobblestone lanes of Dublin's liveliest district, live music spilling out of every doorway.
social.bonus: Talk to someone from a country you've never visited.

chill.title: East Pier and a 99 from Teddy's
chill.description: Walk the granite pier out to the lighthouse in the wind, then join the queue that has been forming outside Teddy's since 1950.
chill.bonus: Get the flake. Always the flake.

chill.title: An Hour in the National Library Reading Room
chill.description: Get a reader's ticket, sit under the domed roof on Kildare Street, and work on something in the room where Joyce set a chapter of Ulysses.
chill.bonus: Bring an actual notebook and write by hand.

chill.title: The Winding Stair, Bottom Then Top
chill.description: Browse the secondhand bookshop on the quays, then take whatever you bought upstairs to the dining room over the Ha'penny Bridge.
chill.bonus: Buy a book by an author you have never heard of.

chill.title: Find the Iveagh Gardens
chill.description: A walled Victorian garden with a cascade and a hedge maze, hidden behind the Concert Hall and somehow still half empty.
chill.bonus: Find the sunken lawn and lie down on it.

chill.title: Glasshouse Hopping at the Botanic Gardens
chill.description: Move between Victorian curvilinear glasshouses in Glasnevin, going from Irish drizzle to full tropical humidity in one step.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest plant in the collection.

chill.title: Explore the Chester Beatty gallery and rooftop garden
chill.description: Wander a free museum of illuminated manuscripts and ancient scrolls, then finish on its quiet rooftop garden overlooking Dublin Castle.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest manuscript on display.

chill.title: Afternoon tea at The Shelbourne
chill.description: Take a formal afternoon tea in one of Dublin's grandest hotels, tiered stands of scones and pastries included.
chill.bonus: Try every single tier of the tea stand before you leave.

chill.title: Sit in the Long Room at Trinity College Library
chill.description: Stand under barrel-vaulted ceilings between two floors of centuries-old leather-bound books.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest book on display and read its title card.

chill.title: Wander St. Stephen's Green at golden hour
chill.description: Loop the paths of Dublin's best-loved city park as the light turns soft over the ponds and flowerbeds.
chill.bonus: Feed the ducks something other than bread.

8ball.title: Get Off the DART Somewhere You've Never Been
8ball.description: Board the coastal line, pick a station you have only ever passed through, and give that town three hours of your day.
8ball.bonus: Swim wherever you end up, weather permitting.

8ball.title: Ask the Bartender Where They Actually Drink
8ball.description: Start anywhere on South William Street, ask the person pouring where they go on their night off, then go there and do it again.
8ball.bonus: Three pubs deep before you are allowed to stop.
